name: Rivastigmine
route_note: Oral capsules or solution twice daily with food; once-daily transdermal patch.
originator: Marta Weinstock-Rosin (Hebrew University of Jerusalem), developed by Sandoz/Novartis

discovery.by: Marta Weinstock-Rosin, Hebrew University of Jerusalem
discovery.note: A carbamate derived from the physostigmine pharmacophore, licensed to Sandoz (later Novartis). Year of the first patent, per Wikipedia (patented 1985, medical use 1997).

tagline: Cholinesterase inhibitor for Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease dementia, also as a patch
summary: Rivastigmine is a carbamate cholinesterase inhibitor used for mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's disease and dementia associated with Parkinson's disease. Its transdermal patch reduces the gastrointestinal effects seen with capsules.
mechanism: Rivastigmine carbamylates the active site of acetylcholinesterase and butyrylcholinesterase, inactivating them for hours; it is therefore termed 'pseudo-irreversible'. This increases acetylcholine availability in cortical and hippocampal synapses.
Because it is hydrolysed by its target enzymes rather than by hepatic cytochrome P450, it has few pharmacokinetic drug interactions.
uses: Mild-to-moderate dementia of the Alzheimer's type
Mild-to-moderate dementia associated with Parkinson's disease
Severe Alzheimer's dementia (13.3 mg/24 h patch, US)

history.title: European approval
history.detail: Exelon is authorised in the EU for Alzheimer's disease.

history.title: EXPRESS trial
history.detail: Emre et al. (NEJM) show benefit in dementia associated with Parkinson's disease.

history.title: Parkinson's disease dementia
history.detail: Rivastigmine becomes the first drug approved for Parkinson's disease dementia in the US and EU.

history.title: Patch
history.detail: The FDA approves the Exelon transdermal patch.

history.title: Severe Alzheimer's
history.detail: The 13.3 mg/24 h patch is approved in the US for severe Alzheimer's disease.

pk.half_life: about 1.5 hours (enzyme inhibition lasts about 10 hours)
pk.bioavailability: about 36% for a 3 mg oral dose
pk.metabolism: hydrolysis by cholinesterases; minimal CYP involvement

serious: Severe vomiting with oesophageal rupture (after dose errors)
Medication errors from applying multiple patches

facts: Rivastigmine is the only cholinesterase inhibitor approved for Parkinson's disease dementia in both the US and EU.
